Title: Open Redirect via Wildcard Redirect URI Validation Bypass
Analysis:
**Source**:
The `redirect_uri` query parameter supplied by the user/attacker in the OIDC authorization endpoint.

**Sanitization/Validation**:
In `RedirectUtils.java`, the `verifyRedirectUri` method validates the user-supplied `redirect_uri` parameter. When comparing against a client-configured redirect URI that uses a wildcard suffix (e.g. `https://test*` or `https://example.com/app*`), it performs a simple `.startsWith()` check after stripping the `*` character.

**Sink**:
The validation uses `r.startsWith(validRedirect)` to approve the redirection. When the wildcard is placed directly at the end of a domain name or path prefix without a trailing slash (e.g. `https://example.com*`), an attacker can construct a domain starting with that prefix (e.g. `https://example.com.attacker.com`) and bypass the validation check. This allows them to steal the authorization code via open redirection.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload**:
Consider a client configured with the valid redirect URI pattern `https://example.com*`.
An attacker can initiate the OIDC authorization flow with:
`GET /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth?client_id={client_id}&response_type=code&redirect_uri=https://example.com.attacker.com/oauth2/callback&state=mystate`

During validation:
1. `validRedirect` is `https://example.com*`.
2. Truncation yields `https://example.com`.
3. `redirect_uri` is `https://example.com.attacker.com/oauth2/callback`.
4. `redirect_uri.startsWith("https://example.com")` evaluates to `true`.
5. Keycloak redirects the user to `https://example.com.attacker.com/oauth2/callback?code=AUTH_CODE&state=mystate`, exposing the authorization code to the attacker.
